column2: The defenders are dead or fled, and the people of [From.GetName] cower in their cellars and barns. My warriors drag them out by the hair and rope them neck to neck: men for the oar and the mine, women and children for the markets. A fine haul. They will fetch a good price, or work my own lands until they drop.

The raid on [From.GetName] has gone well. Chains are hammered shut on the necks of the surviving folk, and they are driven to the black arks to be sold in the markets of Karond Kar, or broken in my own fields and mines. Those who die on the way are thrown to the sea, or kept for the altars of Khaine.
Chain them all. Every one of them has a price.
Their blood belongs to the gods. Kill them on the altar.
Leave them. Their misery is enough.

The slave dealers have come to my pens to haggle: fat men with rings on every finger and whips in their belts, and a scribe to count the heads. The market is as it always is. A lot of captives fetches fifty gold, and they will sell me one for eighty.
Sell a lot.
Sell three lots.
Sell them all.
Not today.

Slaves do not need wages, only whips and bread. A column of my captives can dig the mines and fields of [From.GetName] for years before they are worked to death, though the locals fear them, and fear what happens when they rise.
Put them to work.
Keep them in the pens for now.

The slave dealers have come to my pens to haggle, but they are in no hurry. Every raider on the coast has been selling this season, they say, and the markets are full of captives nobody wants. They will give only thirty-five gold a lot, though they will sell me one for sixty.

The slave dealers have come to my pens in a hurry. War has emptied the markets of hands for the oars, the mines and the fields, and the buyers are hungry. They will pay seventy-five gold a lot, and want a hundred and ten for one of theirs.
You sell every lot in your pens at the market price.
Buy a lot.

The walls of [From.GetName] are ours, and its people are on their knees in the square. Merchants, craftsmen, priests and their families: strong backs and skilled hands, enough for two columns in chains. Some of my captains want to put the town to the sword, others to the torch, but every one of them is worth more alive and sold.
Chain them and march them home.
The gods want their share. All of it.
Leave them be. We came for the walls, not for them.

The overseers woke me before dawn: the slaves have broken out of the pens. A lock was picked, or a guard was bribed or strangled, and now the fields are empty and the dogs are baying in the woods. They cannot have gone far on foot, and they will not know the country.
Saddle the horses and loose the dogs!
The runaways are gone.
Those we catch will be flayed in front of the others.
The slaves worked in your provinces will be cowed for five years: they are less likely to rise.
Let them go. The forests will finish them.

A sickness has broken out in the slave pens: a bloody flux that runs through them like fire through straw. The overseers are afraid to go in, and the dead are piling up at the gate faster than they can be carted off. If nothing is done it will take half of them.
Send for a physician. They are worth more than his fee.
Drag out the sick and burn them, before it spreads.
Let it run its course. The strong will live.

There is one in the pens who will not break. The overseers have whipped [slave_champion.GetHerHim], starved [slave_champion.GetHerHim] and chained [slave_champion.GetHerHim] to the wall, and still [slave_champion.GetSheHe] spits at them and fights. Two of them have broken bones to show for it. The other slaves have begun to whisper [slave_champion.GetHerHis] name, [slave_champion.GetFirstName], and that is a dangerous thing.
Throw [slave_champion.GetHerHim] in the pit. Let [slave_champion.GetHerHim] fight for the crowd.
[slave_champion.GetFirstName] will fight in the pit. Few live, and the one who wins three fights is freed.
Break [slave_champion.GetHerHim]. For good.
Strike off [slave_champion.GetHerHis] chains. I could use someone like that in my guard.

The crowd has not stopped roaring since the third fight. [slave_champion.GetFirstName] killed a fen beast with [slave_champion.GetHerHis] bare hands, then the two best fighters of my slave-masters, and now stands in the sand covered in blood, staring up at my seat. By the custom of the pit [slave_champion.GetSheHe] is free. And the whole land will talk of the games I give.

[slave_champion.GetFirstName] fought like a daemon. [slave_champion.GetSheHeCap] killed the first beast and wounded the second, but the third fight was one too many, and the crowd howled as the slave-masters dragged the body out of the pit. A fine show. The whole land will talk of the games I give, and the other slaves will whisper a little less.
A fine show.

The slaves worked in [From.GetName] have risen. They killed their overseers in the night, broke into the armouries and now march under a former slave, [From.Owner.GetBestName]'s rival in blood. Every chained hand in the land is watching to see what I will do.
Hunt them down. Every one.

The slaves worked in [From.GetName] are gathered in the square, and the chains come off one by one while a priest blesses them. Some weep, some just stand there. The fields and the mines will produce less now, but my conscience, and the gods, will be easier.
Go, and be free.
A slave-master offers to take [From.GetTitledFirstName] off my hands for the markets. Captives with skill fetch the best price. Or I could keep [From.GetHerHim] in my own pens with the rest.
Into the pens with the rest.
You can sell [Root.GetTitledFirstName] in the slave markets for an appropriate sum, or put [Root.GetHerHim] in your pens.
§GOne lot§! of slaves more in your pens.
§GTwo lots§! of slaves more in your pens.
§ROne lot§! of slaves fewer in your pens.
§RTwo lots§! of slaves fewer in your pens.
Slave Pens
A lot or two of slaves fill this lord's pens. Their labour pays.
Full Slave Pens
Three to five lots of slaves fill this lord's pens. Their labour pays well, but the people fear what happens if they rise, and more of them try to run.
Teeming Slave Pens
Six or more lots of slaves crowd this lord's pens. Their labour pays very well, but the people fear them, and escapes and sickness are common.
Slaves Freed
The slaves who worked this province were set free. It is quieter, but poorer.
Slaves Cowed
The slaves worked here saw what was done to the runaways.
Slave Levy Raised
This lord drove a slave levy to war this year.
Slave Dealers Came
The slave dealers have come this half-year.
Broken Chains
Offer Slaves to the Gods
Give a lot of slaves from your pens to the altar.
Raise a Slave Levy
Drive two lots of slaves ahead of your army with spears in their hands and whips at their backs.
§G600 light infantry§! of slaves gather at your capital. They go home, or die, at the peace.
Feed the Forges
Send three lots of slaves into the forges and factories of your capital, to be worked until they drop.
Your capital's slave factory grows by §Gone level§!.
Free the Slaves in Your Pens
Strike the chains off every slave in your pens and let them go.
Every slave in your pens goes free.
Free the Worked Slaves
Your faith keeps no slaves. Free those who work this province.
The Slave Market
Call the slave dealers to your pens to sell or buy captives. They come once every six months.
Set Slaves to Work in [Root.Location.GetName]
Put a lot of slaves to work in this province's fields and mines for fifteen years: more taxes and cheaper building, but more unrest, and they may rise.
